compositionNote: A broad shelter (广) covers grain husks scattering below (隶) — abundant grain safely stored suggests peace and good HEALTH.
poem: A wide roof (广) shelters grain below,
kept safe and dry as seasons go,
well-fed, well-housed, strong and spry —
that's HEALTHY (kāng), standing high!

compositionNote: The speech radical (讠) combines with 井 (jǐng) as a phonetic hint, giving the sound and sense of speaking or explaining.
poem: Words (讠) drop into a deep stone well (井),
echoing out the tales we tell,
open your mouth and let it ring —
that's how to SPEAK (jiǎng): just say the thing!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a curved animal horn

compositionNote: 角 is itself a pictograph — the original drawing of a pointed, ridged animal horn, later extended to mean any pointed corner.
poem: A single picture, sharp and curled,
an animal's horn against the world,
corners poke out, edges appear —
that's a HORN, or corner (jiǎo), here!

components.meaning: to retreat; but (sound hint for jiǎo)

compositionNote: The flesh radical (月) plus 却 (què), used here as a phonetic hint, together point to a part of the body: the foot.
poem: Flesh (月) that won't retreat (却) or flee,
planted firm and steady, see,
down below where two legs connect —
that's the FOOT (jiǎo) you use to trek!

compositionNote: A hand (扌) reaching out, with 妾 (qiè) giving a phonetic hint, gives the sense of receiving or connecting with someone.
poem: A hand (扌) reaches out, warm and true,
greeting guests as they come through,
linking arms, joining a chain —
that's to RECEIVE (jiē), again, again!

compositionNote: Two 'walking' strokes (彳 and 亍, together forming 行) frame 圭 (guī), a phonetic hint, picturing feet moving along a street.

words.meaning: to stroll the streets; go shopping
to go out onto the street

poem: Left foot steps (彳), a jade charm gleams (圭),
right foot follows (亍), or so it seems,
rows of shops where people flow —
that's the STREET (jiē) where crowds all go!

compositionNote: Silk thread (纟) tied around 吉 (jí, 'lucky'), used here as a phonetic hint, gives the idea of tying a knot.
poem: Silk thread (纟) wraps round something lucky (吉),
knotted tight, secure and plucky,
bound together, start to end —
that's how you TIE (jié) a knot, my friend!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a bundle of wood tied round the middle

compositionNote: 束 is an old pictograph showing a bundle of sticks bound tightly at the middle, giving the sense of tying or a bundle.
poem: A bundle of wood, tied round its middle,
sticks held snug, no room to fiddle,
wrapped up tight from end to end —
that's a BUNDLE (shù), a rope its friend!

compositionNote: A knife (刀) cutting an ox's (牛) horn (角) apart pictures the act of dividing something complex — to untie, solve, or explain.
poem: A horn (角), a knife (刀), and an ox (牛) appear,
cutting apart what's tangled here,
slice the knot, make the puzzle clear —
that's to SOLVE (jiě) whatever's near!

components.meaning: to break off; resolute (sound hint for jué)

compositionNote: The ice/water radical (冫) with 夬 (guài), a phonetic hint meaning 'to break off decisively', points to making a firm decision.
poem: Ice (冫) cracks apart, resolute and bold (夬),
the choice is made, the die is told,
no more waiting, no delay —
that's to DECIDE (jué), come what may!

components.meaning: former times; past (sound hint for jiè)

compositionNote: A person (亻) reaching back to the past (昔), used as a phonetic hint, gives the sense of borrowing or lending.
poem: A person (亻) reaches back to olden days (昔),
asking to borrow in so many ways,
lend a book, a cup, a hand —
that's to BORROW (jiè), understand!

components.meaning: village; unit of distance (sound hint for lǐ)

compositionNote: Jade (王) carved along its natural veins, plus 里 (lǐ) as a phonetic hint, gives the sense of pattern, reason, and order.
poem: Jade (王) is carved along its grain,
shaped with logic, not in vain,
ordered like a village clear and neat (里) —
that's the REASON (lǐ) that makes it complete!

meanings.def: long (of time); for a long time

components.meaning: ancient picture of a person being held back or braced, suggesting delay

compositionNote: 久 is an old pictograph of a figure being restrained or braced from behind, drawing out the moment — hence 'a long time'.
poem: A tiny figure, held, delayed,
waiting long while time is stayed,
minutes stretch, the hours accrue —
that's LONG (jiǔ) — it takes a while, it's true!

components.meaning: a simple vertical stroke, like a worn pole

compositionNote: A weathered pole (丨) standing beside the sun (日) that has risen on it day after day suggests something worn with age — OLD.
poem: A pole (丨) beside the sun (日) each day,
weathered, worn, and turning gray,
seen so many suns go by —
that's OLD (jiù): the years pile high!

compositionNote: A mouth (口) wrapped up (勹) into a neat, complete package of words gives the idea of a finished SENTENCE.
poem: Wrapped up (勹) around a mouth (口) so small,
words enclosed, both short and tall,
a thought tied up, complete, construed —
that's a SENTENCE (jù), neatly glued!

meanings.def: to decide; to fix; to set

components.meaning: straight; correct (feet coming to a stop)

compositionNote: Feet coming to a stop (正) under a roof (宀) picture someone settling down — hence 'fixed' or 'certain'.
poem: Under a roof (宀), feet stand firm and true (正),
settled now, with nothing left to do,
the matter's fixed, the plan's in place —
that's DEFINITE (dìng): a settled case!

compositionNote: Water (氵) paired with 曷 (hé), used as a phonetic hint, points to the body craving water — THIRSTY.

words.meaning: to yearn for; to thirst for

poem: Water (氵) longed for, dry throat's plea (曷),
craving a drink so desperately,
parched and dry, wanting more —
that's THIRSTY (kě) down to your core!

meanings.def: a quarter of an hour; a moment

compositionNote: A knife (刂) beside 亥 (hài), used as a phonetic hint, shows the act of cutting marks into something — to CARVE.
poem: A knife (刂) cuts marks by an ancient sign (亥),
carving lines in careful design,
each little notch, a moment's trace —
that's to CARVE (kè), or a MOMENT's space!

compositionNote: A hollow cave (穴) dug by hard work (工), used here as a phonetic hint, gives the idea of empty space.
poem: A cave (穴) dug out by careful work (工),
hollow inside, where shadows lurk,
nothing left but air and space —
that's EMPTY (kōng), an open place!

meanings.def: to adjust; to mix; to blend

compositionNote: Speech (讠) combined with 周 (zhōu, 'cycle'), used as a phonetic hint, points to adjusting or tuning something until it's right.
poem: Words (讠) go round in weekly cycles (周),
tuning, mixing, working through you,
adjust the settings, get it right —
that's to ADJUST (tiáo) both day and night!

meanings.def: for family members; for things with an opening

components.meaning: ancient picture of an open mouth

compositionNote: 口 is itself a pictograph of a simple open mouth, shown as a square opening.
poem: A simple square, open and wide,
a picture of a mouth, open-eyed,
words come out and food goes in —
that's the MOUTH (kǒu) where sounds begin!

compositionNote: Two mouths (口口) wailing above a dog (犬) picture loud, uncontrolled howling — to CRY.
poem: Two mouths (口口) wail like a dog's (犬) sad cry,
howling loud beneath the sky,
tears fall down, the sobs pour through —
that's to CRY (kū), boo-hoo-hoo!

compositionNote: The clothing radical (衤) with 库 (kù, 'warehouse') as an exact phonetic match gives both sound and sense: clothing for the legs.
poem: Clothing (衤) stored inside a warehouse (库),
folded pants, both new and old,
two legs slide in, side by side —
that's your PANTS (kù) you wear with pride!

compositionNote: Bamboo (竹) paired with 快 (kuài, 'fast'), an exact phonetic match, names the quick bamboo sticks used for eating.
poem: Bamboo (竹) sticks, quick (快) and light,
picking up your food just right,
two thin sticks that work as one —
CHOPSTICKS (kuài) make the eating fun!

compositionNote: The grass radical (艹), for the indigo plant once used to make dye, combines with 监 (jiān) as a phonetic hint to give BLUE.
poem: A plant (艹) once watched with careful eye (监),
dyed indigo beneath the sky,
color of the sea and air —
that's the color BLUE (lán) laid bare!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a tiger, showing its head, stripes, and legs

compositionNote: 虎 is an old pictograph drawn to resemble a standing tiger with its open mouth and striped body.
poem: Stripes and claws in ancient guise,
a fearsome shape before your eyes,
king of the jungle, bold and true —
that's the TIGER (hǔ) stalking you!

components.meaning: a simplified curling stroke standing in for the original phonetic 豊

compositionNote: The altar radical (礻), for ritual and worship, combines with a simplified stroke (乚) replacing the old phonetic 豊, giving CEREMONY.
poem: An altar (礻) bows with a curling line (乚),
offerings placed, a sacred sign,
manners shown and gifts bestowed —
that's the CEREMONY (lǐ) that's owed!

components.meaning: do not (exact sound match for wù)

compositionNote: An ox (牛) beside 勿 (wù, 'do not'), an exact phonetic match, broadened over time to mean any THING or object.
poem: An ox (牛) warned back by a do-not sign (勿),
yet still it works the whole day's time,
creatures, goods, and things at hand —
that's a THING (wù) across the land!

compositionNote: Under a cliff (厂), strength (力) is exerted step by step through time — giving the sense of passing through, or HISTORY.
poem: Under a cliff (厂), with strength (力) to spare,
trudging through the years, everywhere,
seasons passed and days gone by —
that's HISTORY (lì) reaching high!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a hand holding a recording tool, like a scribe keeping records

compositionNote: 史 pictures a hand grasping a document or brush — the ancient scribe who recorded events, giving us HISTORY.
poem: A steady hand holds a scribe's own tool,
recording facts by an ancient rule,
writing down what's come to pass —
that's HISTORY (shǐ), built to last!

compositionNote: The flesh radical (月) with 佥 (qiān), used as a phonetic hint, points to the fleshy part where all your features meet — the FACE.
poem: Flesh (月) shaped smooth, all brought together (佥),
features formed to last forever,
eyes and nose and mouth in place —
that's your FACE (liǎn), your own true face!

meanings.def: to practice; to train; to drill

components.meaning: east (simplified stand-in for the original phonetic 柬)

compositionNote: Thread (纟) that must be worked and pulled repeatedly, with 东 replacing the old phonetic 柬, gives the sense of PRACTICE.
poem: Thread (纟) pulled taut, looped and refined (东),
worked again till it's aligned,
drill it daily, don't give in —
that's to PRACTICE (liàn) till you win!

compositionNote: The vehicle radical (车) with 两 (liǎng, 'two'), a close phonetic hint, gives the measure word used for counting vehicles.
poem: A cart (车) counted, one then two (两),
lined up waiting in a queue,
count them all along the road —
that's the word for CARS (liàng), each load!

compositionNote: An ear (耳) leaning in, with 卯 (mǎo) as a phonetic hint, points to listening closely while chatting.
poem: An ear (耳) leans in at a certain call (卯),
listening close to hear it all,
words flow easy, back and forth —
that's to CHAT (liáo), south and north!

components.meaning: order; command (close sound hint for lín)

compositionNote: 令 (lìng), a close phonetic hint, combines with the settlement radical (阝) to mean someone living in the same settlement — NEIGHBOR.
poem: An order given (令) near your place (阝),
living close, right by your space,
just next door, not far to roam —
that's your NEIGHBOR (lín), near your home!

meanings.def: to reside; to live (in a place)

components.meaning: a reclining person; body (suggests a dwelling)

compositionNote: A reclining figure (尸), suggesting someone settled at home, combines with 古 (gǔ) as a phonetic hint to mean RESIDE.
poem: A reclining form (尸) from days of old (古),
settled down as the story's told,
making a home, staying put —
that's to RESIDE (jū), putting down foot!
